events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven's pier** if you must pick one. Expect slow fishing, about a 1 of 4.
- **Rough ratings for pier salmon this week:** Grand Haven 1, St. Joseph 1, South Haven 1 (a guess, since there's no pier data), Muskegon 0.
- **Don't count on the pier.** The best salmon fishing reported this week was from boats, so if the pier is slow, the boat option is where the reports point.
- **Check the pier before you drive.** The Grand Haven and Muskegon reports are a week old and the surface water has been warm.

## Why
- The Sept 7 Grand Haven report says the pier was slow for salmon, and the Sept 7 Muskegon report says no salmon were reported from the breakwalls (Grand Haven, 2022-09-07; Muskegon, 2022-09-07).
- Grand Haven has the most pier reports of the four ports, and its earlier pier reports were also weak, at 1 (Grand Haven, 2022-08-17; Grand Haven, 2022-08-24).
- I'd expect the pier to stay slow for now because the surface water is still around 72-73 F, well above the 52-58 F range that Chinook and coho prefer (NY DEC reference). That likely keeps the fish deeper and away from the piers.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is 2022-09-07, six days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2022-09-07: boat quality 2, "The pier action was slow for salmon." Quality 0.
- Muskegon, 2022-09-07: boat quality 2 in 60-120 ft, fish 45-90 ft down. Pier: "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls." Quality 0.
- South Haven, 2022-09-07: boat quality 3 ("pretty good fishing this week") in 40-120 ft. No pier report.
- St. Joseph, 2022-09-07: boat quality 1, "Salmon anglers were catching fish when they could get on the lake." No pier report.
- Pier reports before that are sparse. St. Joseph (2022-08-17) had "a few Chinook caught" from the pier, mostly steelhead, and quality 1. Grand Haven (2022-08-17 and 2022-08-24) had coho at quality 1. South Haven had no pier report in the last four weeks.

**Past seasons (history)**
- Searching past seasons at similar surface temperatures (within 3 F of 72 F, within 21 days) returned only the same 2022-09-07 reports. I have no separate history to compare, so these ratings rest mainly on this season's sparse pier data.

**Conditions now**
- Measured buoy surface water (most recent week): St. Joseph 73 F (down 3 F), South Haven 72 F (down 1 F), Grand Haven 72 F (down 1 F), Muskegon 72 F (down 1 F). None of these is a sharp drop, so there's no clear upwelling sign.
- Live data was unavailable. I have no modeled pierhead temperature, no cold-layer depth, and no wind forecast for this week.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are from 2022-09-07, six days old, and conditions can change quickly in fall.
- The ratings are my estimates from sparse, mostly boat-focused reports. South Haven and St. Joseph have almost no pier data, so treat those numbers as the least reliable.
- The live water and weather data was unavailable, so I could not check the modeled pierhead temperature, any upwelling, or the wind. Check the wind before you go; a north or east wind can bring cold water to the piers.

## Sources
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 7: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0 (also covers South Haven and St. Joseph)
- Aug 24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
- Aug 17: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3288194
